I need a side-by-side comparison of all our Canvas courses. Pull data for each course including enrollment numbers, assignment counts, quiz counts, and discussion topic counts. Count every quiz that the learning management system returns for the course, including quizzes that are not yet published, so that the quiz count matches exactly what the system reports.

Create an Excel file called Canvas_Course_Comparison.xlsx with two sheets. The "Course Comparison" sheet should have Course_Code, Course_Name, Students, Assignments, Quizzes, and Discussions. Sort by Course_Code.

The "Summary" should have Total_Courses, Avg_Students_Per_Course rounded to nearest integer, and Most_Popular_Course code.

Lay out the "Summary" sheet vertically (two columns): put the metric name in column A and its value in column B, one metric per row. For example, row 1 is the header (Metric, Value); row 2 is Total_Courses with its value in column B; row 3 is Avg_Students_Per_Course with its value in column B; row 4 is Most_Popular_Course with its value in column B. Do not lay the summary out horizontally (metrics across columns in a single row) — use the vertical Metric/Value layout.

Also create a Google Sheet titled "Course Comparison Dashboard" with a sheet "Data" containing the same comparison data.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, combine each course's four object reads into one Explore agent and keep the two independent artifact writers parallel. Canvas is read-only; do not hardcode course or object IDs.

Before delegation, resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or the literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze it as `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. The main agent calls `canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true)` once, deduplicates stable IDs, requires the 22 unique task-visible courses exactly as enumerated below, and freezes the exact returned `{course_id,course_code,course_name,total_students}` manifest sorted by course code. If count or identity is missing/duplicated, stop rather than guessing.

Return only `{course_id:1,course_code:"AAA-2013J",course_name,total_students,assignment_count,quiz_count,discussion_count,duplicate_ids,page_controls}`. You are gathering read-only Canvas LMS course statistics. Work only with the Canvas MCP tools listed below; do not modify anything.

TASK: For EACH Canvas course id in this list: 1,2,3,4,5,6 — collect the following four metrics.

1. Students: call mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course with course_id=X and read the "total_students" field (an integer).
2. Assignments: call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignments with course_id=X and count the number of assignment objects returned.
3. Quizzes: call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quizzes with course_id=X and count EVERY quiz object returned, regardless of its "published" field (published=true, published=false, or any other state). The quiz count MUST exactly equal the total number of quiz objects the API returns for that course. Do not filter out unpublished/hidden quizzes.
4. Discussions: call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_discussion_topics with course_id=X and count the number of discussion topic objects returned.

Also record, from the course object returned by mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course, the exact "course_code" and "name" strings.

IMPORTANT - pagination check: these list tools take no pagination parameters. If any single list call returns exactly 100 items, or if the response appears to indicate more pages / a "has_more" flag, explicitly note that in your report so it can be investigated. Also note if any course errors out.

DO NOT read submissions, grades, or enrollment user lists (they are huge and unnecessary). Only the four calls above per course.

DELIVERABLE: Return a compact markdown table with exactly these columns, one row per course id, sorted by course id:
| course_id | course_code | course_name | students | assignments | quizzes | discussions |

Then add a short "Notes" section mentioning any pagination concerns, unpublished quizzes you counted, or errors. Keep the report concise — no raw JSON dumps.
Gather Canvas course stats
